description: Live cricket scores, fixtures, and fantasy data from CricAPI / Cricket Data, with offline SQLite and the first cricket MCP server.

novel_features.name: Team-aware fixture filter
novel_features.description: Resolve a team name to all matches involving that team — answers 'when does Pakistan play next?'
novel_features.rationale: CricAPI's /matches endpoint takes a freeform search; no existing CLI applies that filter cleanly across upcoming + recent in one shot.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Translates the natural-language cricket query an agent or user most often asks into a single command, instead of forcing them to browse a fixture list manually.

novel_features.name: Today's matches with format filter
novel_features.description: Live and about-to-start matches now, with optional --format filter (t20i, odi, test, t20, t10, hundred)
novel_features.rationale: currentMatches returns everything mixed; the format filter is where CLI ergonomics actually win over the website.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Single command gives the agent the right shape of 'what's on right now' without paginating the whole match list.

novel_features.name: Live match watch loop
novel_features.description: Poll a match score on a loop with configurable interval; prints state changes
novel_features.rationale: No CricAPI endpoint pushes updates; a server-side watch is the only way to follow a match without manual refresh.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Keeps an agent in the loop on a live match without burning calls when nothing changes — only prints on score-state changes.

novel_features.name: Local series watchlist
novel_features.description: Track favourite series under friendly aliases; refresh all in one shot
novel_features.rationale: CricAPI has no concept of a user's followed series; the local store fills that gap entirely.
novel_features.example:
cricapi-pp-cli watchlist add ipl abc-series-id
cricapi-pp-cli watchlist refresh
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets the user pin a tournament once and refresh on demand — no other cricket CLI maintains local state at all.
